diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, from Monotonocity Principle for the NtD operator stated in~\ref{prop:mono}, it follows that $\Lambda_{\sigma_D}-\Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}}\geqslant 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The recalled 'well known inequality' is false as displayed. Since the NtD map is monotonically decreasing (Property prop:mono), with the substitution used in the proof (sigma_1 = sigma_D <= sigma_bg = sigma_2, insulating anomaly) the middle term satisfies <(Lambda_{sigma_D}-Lambda_{sigma_bg})g,g> >= 0, while both displayed bounds are <= 0 (they carry the factor sigma_1 - sigma_2 <= 0); the display would force <(Lambda_{sigma_D}-Lambda_{sigma_bg})g,g> = 0 for every g, contradicting the positivity asserted two lines later in the same proof and the strictly positive eigenvalues lambda_k computed in Section 5. The step 'from (eqn:in1) we have (eqn:lem1)' thus silently reverses the inequalities. The correctly oriented estimate (int_D (sigma_bg - sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 dx <= <(Lambda_{sigma_D}-Lambda_{sigma_bg})g,g> <= int_D (sigma_bg/sigma_a)(sigma_bg - sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 dx) is displayed, correctly signed, in Section 6; with it the proof of the lemma goes through verbatim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed inequality by its correctly oriented form, i.e. the two-sided estimate already displayed in Section 6 (int_D (sigma_bg - sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 dx <= <(Lambda_{sigma_D}-Lambda_{sigma_bg})g,g> <= int_D (sigma_bg/sigma_a)(sigma_bg - sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 dx), and keep the remainder of the proof unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of lem:mainl is invalid as written. The lemma's statement itself is true, and no other labelled result relies on the flawed step, since the correctly signed version of the same estimate appears later in Section 6.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma 3.1 rests on a monotonicity estimate recalled with reversed signs
issues.why_classification: A local replacement of the misquoted inequality by the correctly oriented standard estimate repairs the proof; the lemma's conclusion, the constant k_1 and all downstream claims survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega$ be a connected open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $n = 2,3$, and $A\subset\Omega$, and $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ solution of
Indeed, if $u_{bg}$ is constant in $D$, then it results to be constant over $\Omega$ and, consequently, on $\partial \Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: A is an arbitrary subset of Omega with no hypothesis (e.g. nonempty interior or positive measure). For A with empty interior, such as a single point or A = empty set, every solution u is 'constant in A', so the statement as written would imply that every solution of the conductivity equation on a connected domain is constant; this is false (take sigma = 1 and u(x) = x_1 on a connected Omega, which is constant on A = {0} but not on Omega). The standard weak UCP requires A to contain a nonempty open set. The paper only applies the result with A = D_i (open connected sets), so the intended use is not affected.

failure_location.quote: If $u$ is constant in $A$, then $u$ is constant in $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that A has nonempty interior (or is open), as in the cited references.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem teo:ucp is false as stated. Its only use in the paper (Section 3, with A = D_i) is covered by the corrected statement, so no labelled result is invalidated.
issues.title: Weak UCP stated for an arbitrary set A, so the theorem is false as stated
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard local hypothesis repairs the statement; the application with A = D_i and the following UCP-based argument are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\lambda_k$, $\tilde{\lambda}_k$ the eigenvalues of $\Lambda_{\sigma_D}-\Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}}$ and $\Lambda_n$, respectively, ordered in a decreasing order.

issues.failure_explanation: With N only bounded, Lambda_n = A + N (A compact self-adjoint) need not be self-adjoint: its spectrum need not be real, need not consist of eigenvalues, and 'ordered in a decreasing order' is undefined, so the asserted Weyl-type matching |tilde lambda_k - lambda_k| <= ||N|| is not a valid statement under the stated hypotheses (e.g. N = i*delta*I is bounded with ||N|| = delta and shifts the whole spectrum off the real line). The bound is Weyl's inequality, valid when N = N*, which is the case for the noise matrix (A + A^T)/2 used in the numerical section.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that N is self-adjoint (N = N*); the inequality then follows from Weyl's min-max inequality applied to the compact self-adjoint operators Lambda_{sigma_D} - Lambda_{sigma_bg} and Lambda_n.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:pert is not valid under its stated hypotheses; the subsequent discussion of noise-corrupted eigenvalues is justified only for self-adjoint noise, which is what the numerical model actually uses.
issues.title: Eigenvalue perturbation bound asserted for a merely bounded, not necessarily self-adjoint, noise operator
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard hypothesis (N = N*, satisfied by the noise actually used) restores the statement with no loss of guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: From the displayed (correct) two-sided estimate only the upper bound of (eqn:sogp3) follows, via (sigma_bg - sigma_a)/sigma_bg >= Delta_sigma/sigma_bg^M. The lower bound int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2 dx >= (sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma) Q would require Q <= (Delta_sigma/sigma_a^m) int_D sigma_bg |grad u_bg|^2 dx, but the estimate gives Q <= int_D (sigma_bg/sigma_a)(sigma_bg - sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 dx, and pointwise (sigma_bg - sigma_a)/sigma_a <= (sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m)/sigma_a^m, not <= Delta_sigma/sigma_a^m = (sigma_bg^m - sigma_a^M)/sigma_a^m; the two bounds coincide only for essentially constant coefficients. Concrete admissible counterexample: sigma_bg = 10 on D and 1 on Omega\D, sigma_a = 0.9 (sigma_a^M = 0.9 < sigma_bg^m = 1, well separated, Delta_sigma = 0.1). The exact identity Q = int_D (sigma_bg - sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 dx + int_Omega sigma_D|grad(u_D - u_bg)|^2 dx gives Q >= 0.91 * int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2, i.e. int_D p <= Q/0.91, while the claim demands int_D p >= 9 Q; violated for every excitation with Q > 0 (such excitations exist, e.g. boundary modes). Consequently the alpha-range in (eqn:thr) and the following remark's criterion for alpha = 1 are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the bounds from the two-sided estimate already displayed in the same section, using (sigma_bg - sigma_a)/sigma_a <= (sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m)/sigma_a^m, which yields (sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M - sigma_a^m))(P-P_b) <= int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2 dx <= (sigma_bg^m/Delta_sigma)(P-P_b); restate (eqn:thr) and the remark accordingly (or restrict the claim to essentially constant sigma_a and sigma_bg, where the displayed constants are correct).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised analytic bounds for admissible thresholds and the alpha-range of (eqn:thr), together with the following remark's easy criterion, are invalid; the final algorithm's integral condition (eqn:thr2), which does not use alpha, is not affected.
issues.title: Lower bound in the threshold estimate (eqn:sogp3) fails for non-constant coefficients
issues.why_classification: A contained re-derivation with corrected constants, using only the two-sided estimate already present in the source, restores a comparable guarantee; but the advertised admissible-alpha criterion and the remark's easy test materially change, so the repair exceeds a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, the Unique Continuation Principle (UCP), which has a central role for Elliptic PDEs, prevents the existence of this special boundary data $g$.
As a direct consequence of the UCP stated in Theorem~\ref{teo:ucp}, it is not possible to find a non-constant boundary data $g$ fulfilling~\eqref{eqn:idcond}.

we search for a boundary data $g$ that is a good approximation of an element of $\ker\{\Lambda_{\sigma_D}-\Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}}\}$, in the sense that it is able to make the power difference $\langle\left(\Lambda_{\sigma_D}-\Lambda_{\sigma_{bg}}\right)g,g\rangle$ arbitrary small.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusions state that the method 'relies on the possibility to find' a boundary data g producing a vanishing electric field in the anomaly and that the paper provides 'a simple manner to evaluate this special boundary data g'. The paper's own UCP argument establishes that no non-trivial such g exists (ker{Lambda_{sigma_D} - Lambda_{sigma_bg}} = {0}), and what the algorithm actually computes is an eigenfunction of the (noisy) difference operator making the power difference small, i.e. an approximation of the effect, never the special data itself. The prose therefore claims more than the formal content establishes.

failure_location.quote: We provide a simple manner to evaluate this special boundary data $g$ and from this we derive a new algorithm with a very simple numerical implementation and very low computational cost.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to state that the paper provides a simple way to compute a boundary data approximating an element of the kernel (making the power difference small).
issues.overall_effect: Only the summary description of the contribution in Section 8 is misleading; no theorem, guarantee or algorithmic step is invalidated.
issues.title: Conclusions claim the special boundary data g is evaluated, although the paper proves it does not exist
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of an overclaim removes the defect; all formal content and guarantees are preserved.
